newsitem.title: UK: Tesco results outshone by sales gain.
newsitem.headline: Tesco results outshone by sales gain.

text.p: Britain's leading supermarket chain Tesco Plc reported an 11 percent jump in profits on Tuesday but what pleased the market most was a healthy boost in sales and prospects of more to come.
"There were no surprises in the headline figures but the second-half trading news was pretty well received," one dealer said.

Profit before tax in the six months ending Aug. 10 rose to 321 million pounds ($498 million) from 290 million pounds ($453 million) last year, on a 14 percent rise in gross sales to 6.72 billion pounds ($10.5 billion).

The company said comparable store sales were currently running 7.5 percent ahead of last year after a 7 percent increase in the first half, and Chairman Sir Ian MacLaurin said he expected more to come.
"I would expect us to (be above 7.5 percent)," he said.

MacLaurin said in a statement that Tesco, which has overtaken arch-rival J. Sainsbury Plc in terms of market share and currently holds 14 percent, would continue to develop its business and believed it would be able to maintain its momentum.
